result:
Done — everything typechecks and the full suite passes (6 tests, including 4 new ones), and I verified the real dev path end-to-end: a registration against the booted app with `QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync`/`MAIL_MAILER=log` prints `Subject: Welcome to Guren, Grace Hopper!` to the terminal, and with `QUEUE_CONNECTION=memory`/`MAIL_MAILER=memory` the request leaves exactly one job waiting and zero messages sent until the job is run.

I brought up the queue and mailer the way this project does it (`bunx guren add queue` / `add mail`, which the README points at, then adapted the scaffolding to the `.env` this app ships): `app/Providers/QueueProvider.ts` builds a QueueManager whose default connection is `QUEUE_CONNECTION` (`sync` inline, `memory` held for a worker; an unknown name fails loudly at boot rather than silently running production work in-request), registers `SendWelcomeEmailJob`, and publishes the driver `Job.dispatch()` pushes to unless one is already installed; `app/Providers/MailProvider.ts` builds a MailManager whose default transport is `MAIL_MAILER` (`log`/`memory`/`resend`) with `from` taken from `MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS`/`MAIL_FROM_NAME`, binds it as the container's `mail`, and installs it via `setMailManager()` so out-of-request work can reach it; both are wired into `src/app.ts` after the framework's own `QueueServiceProvider`/`MailServiceProvider`. `app/Mail/WelcomeMail.ts` builds the message — subject `Welcome to ${APP_NAME}, ${name}!` read from the environment, plain-text greeting by name — and `app/Jobs/SendWelcomeEmailJob.ts` resolves the mail manager and sends it when the job runs, retrying up to three attempts. `RegisterController.store()` now ends with `await SendWelcomeEmailJob.dispatch({ name, email })` after the user is created and signed in, so a refused registration (validation error or taken email) throws earlier and queues nothing; the redirect to `/dashboard` is unchanged. Tests live in `tests/RegisterWelcomeEmail.test.ts` (fake queue + fake mail transport, covering queued-not-sent, the delivered message after running the job, and both refusal paths), and I noted the new `app/Jobs/` and `app/Mail/` directories plus the welcome-mail flow in the README. One thing I deliberately left out: the `redis` queue driver that `.env` documents for production is not registered — wiring it needs `ioredis`, which is only present as a transitive dependency, so I left a pointer in `QueueProvider` instead of adding an undeclared dependency; dispatching code is unaffected either way.
